title: Esra's Brilliant Heat Shield
markdown:
Dawn exploded through Esra’s window. Winter Shelter Contest day. She rocketed out of bed, her room buzzing with blueprints. Captain Noor had stressed the science: understand how heat behaves.

Esra dashed to the workshop. Her first shelter, a blanket-filled cube, failed instantly. Heat just leaked out. A solid plastic wall didn’t help. Heat vanished faster than she could track.

Then she watched Mica, her cat, curled tight, fur puffed out. Mica’s fur trapped air, keeping him toasty. “Mica,” Esra whispered, “you’re a genius.”

It clicked. Mica’s fur held air pockets. Her shelter’s heat was moving — touching walls, slipping through. Tiny air currents swirled inside. Heat was beaming out like invisible rays. Her cube was a heat highway.

With fierce determination, Esra built. Thin panels formed the shell. Mica’s fluffy socks stuffed between the walls trapped air. A baffled entrance blocked easy convection. She kept the outside pale, to throw back radiation, and placed the tiny heat lamp so the interior could take that warmth and hold it. Comforting warmth. Her temperature gauge climbed. “Yes!”

Captain Noor grinned. “Looking good, Esra. What principles?”

Esra beamed. “Managing heat transfer. The socks trap air to slow conduction and convection. The baffles stop the draught. The pale shell cuts radiative loss. Not a magic box. A set of small refusals.”

Noor chuckled. “Understanding heat is key. Spacesuits use layers for the same reasons — trap, block the swirl, reflect what would otherwise fly away.”

Esra felt a thrill. The shelter was built. The science was clear. She was ready. She looked at Mica, still a loaf of trapped air, and wondered what other quiet highways heat was taking, just out of sight.
characters: Esra (an astronomy intern), Mica (a cat), Noor (a captain)
